verdicts.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
verdicts.reason: The official NJ DCA Truth in Renting guide states there is no statewide rent control or rent-increase cap. Rent control is left to municipal ordinances. The guide also notes that increases must not be 'unconscionable' under the Anti-Eviction Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f)), but that is a case-by-case judicial standard rather than a statutory cap. The retrieved passages concern other jurisdictions (CA, MA) and do not bear on NJ.
